title: SDK footprint minimizer: onramp notes and lightweight quickstart
body:
Purpose:
This is an exploratory working doc for a tiny-first SDK onramp: reduce install size, runtime startup cost, and warmup latency for Redwood customers that embed the SDK in browser or edge apps. Goal is a pragmatic quickstart that gets engineers sending 1st requests with <100KB gzipped SDK + minimal polyfills, and provides telemetry hooks to measure first-3-requests latency delta.

Context and motivation:
- Many customers embed our JS/TS SDK in web UIs, extension hosts, mobile webviews, and serverless edge functions where download + startup cost dominates UX.
- Current SDK bundles are ~350-500KB gz (varies by build targets). We need a lightweight path for latency-sensitive flows (autocomplete, instant answers, inline generation).
- This doc sketches a minimal onramp and checklist for an official "light" release channel and a lab-run to validate UX improvements.

Design constraints (non-negotiable):
1) API parity for generation/streaming endpoints used in first-run examples (same runtime API surface but lazy-loaded helpers).
2) No breaking changes to existing public API; prefer new entrypoint (import '@redwood/sdk/light' or import('@redwood/sdk/light').then(...)).
3) Compat with ES module loaders, modern browsers, and popular bundlers (esbuild/rollup/webpack/vite).
4) Tree-shakeable: avoid global side-effects, use named exports, prefer function factories.
5) Telemetry: expose optional instrumentation hooks (subscribe to send/recv, timing marks) without shipping telemetry back to our servers by default.

Minimal quickstart flow (developer facing) — copyable in README:
1) npm install @redwood/sdk-light --save
2) import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-light'
3) const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
4) // first-call pattern
5) const stream = await client.chat.stream({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize roadmap' }] })
6) stream.on('data', chunk => appendToUI(chunk.text))

Quickstart implementation notes (internal):
- Provide a single minimal entrypoint which dynamically imports heavy pieces only when needed:
  export async function createClient(cfg) {
    const platform = await import('./platform-lite.js')
    const runtime = await import('./runtime-core.js') // small core
    return runtime.init(platform.default, cfg)
  }
- Keep base runtime ~25-40KB gz (ESM, no polyfills). Move helpers (retry/backoff, rich response parsing, websocket fallback) into optional modules loaded on demand.
- Provide a tiny polyfill detector shim that only pulls polyfills if feature-detection fails (e.g., structuredClone, fetch streaming).
- Offer a Wasm path for constrained runtimes where binary sizes are better (explore later).

Telemetry and measurement plan (how we'll prove impact):
Metric set (for lab and customer opt-in):
- SDK payload size (gzip/brotli) by entrypoint and by bundler target.
- Cold startup time measured as time-to-sdk-initialized (SDK init to ready-to-send).
- First-request RTT (client send to first-byte-of-model-response).
- First-3-requests delta: median latency of first 3 requests vs steady-state after 10 requests.
- Page time-to-interactive (TTI) improvement when SDK is part of initial bundle.

Measurement harness:
- Provide a small synthetic harness in /labs/light-harness that simulates typical page flows and records marks using Performance.mark().
- Lightweight instruction: open http://localhost:8080/harness?scenario=autocomplete, open devtools, run harness to record marks, harness uploads JSON to local server for analysis.

Developer experience: checklist for the light quickstart doc:
- [ ] Short explanation of when to choose light vs full SDK (use cases and tradeoffs).
- [ ] Install snippet for npm/yarn/pnpm and CDN usage (unpkg/cdn.jsdelivr) with ESM import map example.
- [ ] Quick troubleshooting section: common bundler pitfalls (duplicate fetch polyfill, top-level await, SSR hydration warnings).
- [ ] Example for lazy-loading in React/Vue/Svelte + suggested hook patterns (useRedwoodClient lazy initializer).
- [ ] Migration note for existing heavy SDK users: alias examples in package.json to switch to light channel for hotfix experiments.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Where do we draw the line on retry/backoff? Many customers need robust retries; moving retries to optional module may increase user friction. Propose default: very small retry shim (exponential backoff w/ one retry) in core, full policy in optional package.
- CDN ESM support: verify size and integrity when served as module across browsers.
- Security review: ensure dynamic import pattern does not open up CSP or SRI compatibility issues.
- Telemetry opt-in UX: simplest is a createClient({ telemetry: false }) default; enabling returns a telemetry object with flush() method.

Lab run plan (2-week spike):
Week 0 (prep): pick 3 customer-like scenarios: autocomplete in SPA, inline assistant in help center, edge function summarizer.
Week 1 (build): implement sdk-light entrypoint, basic lazy import paths, and a harness for measurements.
Week 2 (validate): run harness across Chrome/headless, Node edge runtimes, and vary bundler settings. Collect metrics and draft short results note.

Acceptance criteria for promoting light channel to "experimental release":
- gzipped SDK entry < 150KB for typical ESM consumer scenario.
- median first-request delta reduced by >=30% in SPA autocomplete scenario compared to full SDK.
- no regressions in streaming behavior (end-to-end functional smoke tests pass).
- documented migration steps and two short example projects updated.

Sample dev notes (command snippets):
- Build locally (esbuild):
  npx esbuild src/light-entry.ts --bundle --format=esm --minify --sourcemap=false --outfile=dist/light-entry.mjs
- Produce gz size:
  gzip -c dist/light-entry.mjs | wc -c
- Run harness:
  cd labs/light-harness && npm i && npm run dev && open http://localhost:8080

UX copy ideas for README quick blurb:
"Redwood SDK — Light channel. Tiny install, lazy features. Same API for sending requests; optimized for instant-first-character experiences. Use when you care about download and startup latency over full feature set."

Notes to self / meeting agenda for follow-up with Marcus/Asha (Mar 6):
- Walk through lazy-import architecture and verify no unexpected circular deps.
- Discuss minimal retry policy in core vs optional module.
- Validate telemetry opt-in shapes and API (flush, subscribe, attachTraceId).
- Decide on naming: @redwood/sdk-light vs @redwood/sdk/esm-light or scoped entrypoint.

Appendix: small heuristics checklist for reviewers:
- Avoid large deps: lodash, moment, axios. Prefer native APIs or tiny helpers.
- Prefer native fetch + ReadableStream for streaming tokenization.
- Export minimal type defs for TypeScript users to get autocompletion without full compile-time cost.
- Document how to run local smoke test with a stubbed server (example in labs/stubs).

Unresolved: how aggressively to support legacy browsers (IE/old Safari). For MVP, target evergreen browsers and Node 18+ for edge functions.

End of draft.
summary: Working draft for a minimal 'light' SDK onramp: architecture, quickstart, measurement plan, lab run, and open questions. Aimed at reducing SDK download and cold-start latency for browser/edge use cases.
